topics.title: Equations and Inequalities
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Build formula from word statements. (u, s)
Re-write a given formula by changing the subject. (u, s)
Solve equations and inequalities, representing the solutions on a number line or graphically as appropriate. (k, u, s)

body.text: Turning a word problem into a formula means naming the unknowns and writing their relationship as an equation. Ruth is r years old; Bayo is one year older than Ruth, so Bayo's age = r+1. John's age is 3 times Bayo's age, so John's age = 3(r+1) = 3r+3.

Changing the subject of a formula means rearranging it to isolate a different variable, using the same balance method as solving equations. Given the formula v = u + at (final velocity), rearrange to make t the subject: subtract u from both sides to get v-u = at, then divide both sides by a to get t = (v-u)/a.

body.expr: v = u + at   ->   v - u = at   ->   t = (v-u)/a

body.text: This year's work extends inequalities (Senior 2, Topic 5) to quadratics. Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 <= 0: first solve the equation x^2-5x+6=0 to get x=2 and x=3 (the graph's roots), then check the sign of the parabola between and outside these roots — since it opens upward, the expression is negative (≤0) between the roots, so the solution is 2 <= x <= 3.
